newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico state governor says to sue NY Times, DEA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico state governor says to sue NY Times, DEA.

text.p: A Mexican state governor accused in a New York Times article this week of having links to drug-trafficking said on Thursday he planned to sue the newspaper throught the Mexican courts.

"Gov. Manlio Fabio Beltrones has decided to sue in civil and penal court the newspaper The New York Times (and) the reporters Samuel Dillon and Craig Pyes," the government of Sonora state said in a statement.

Beltrones would also sue "the foreign individuals and organisations and the agents of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) quoted in the article, who provided this news medium with false and baseless information," the statement said.
The suits would be filed in Mexican courts, it added.
Dillon, one of the newspaper's Mexico-based correspondents, declined to comment to Reuters.

The newspaper, citing U.S. officials and intelligence sources, said in its Sunday edition that Beltrones had helped create a haven for smugglers who ship vast quantities of drugs into the United States but that he enjoyed political immunity.
The governor of Morelos state, Jorge Carrillo Olea, was also on a U.S. blacklist because of reported links with major drug dealers, the paper said.
Carrillo said on Wednesday that he too was planning to sue the newspaper.
